title: Operator checklist for latency-sensitive A/B runs (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Short working notes for engineers/operators running A/B experiments where latency is a first-class constraint.
- Focus: experiments that touch routing, model variants, and hybrid inference (hosted + dedicated).
- Intended audience: release lead, oncall, SRE, product steward.

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing transient latency regressions during medium-to-large traffic ramps.
- Existing rollout playbooks focus on safety signals, not operator steps for fast mitigation of token-latency spikes.
- This doc is an intentionally terse operator checklist + quick heuristics to use while we formalize a full runbook.

Quick glossary (operator shorthand):
- A: control variant (current production routing)
- B: experiment variant (new model / routing policy / quantized runtime)
- TTF: token-time-per-forward (proxy metric from runtime traces)
- P50/P95/P99: latency percentiles over token or request depending on metric
- KV-hit-rate: cache hit ratio for prefix/KV caching

Pre-run checklist (30–60m before exposure):
- Confirm run owner + emergency contact in the experiment header.
- Validate smoky baseline: snapshot production P95 and P99 for last 30m, token-level and request-level.
- Ensure dedicated telemetry streams: route-tagged traces, sample payloads, and debug token-level traces enabled for slices.
- Canary seed: pick 0.1% user-cohort with high signal-to-noise (heavy RPC users, internal traffic). Avoid first-time users and mobile users for initial seed.
- Capacity probe: run synthetic traffic at 2x median concurrency for 5m against B in isolated test cluster. Watch GPU mem, kernel stalls, and queue length.
- Verify fallback policy exists: model variant fallback + region fallback + per-request fallback to synchronous host model.
- Ensure ops channels: #release-ops, #sre, and direct SMS to oncall.

Ramp plan (example):
- 0.1% (seed) for 20–30m -> 1% for 15m -> 5% for 15m -> 20% for 30m -> 100% continue only if signals green.
- Stop criteria evaluated at every step. If any stop criteria hit, immediately trigger rollback to A and escalate.

Stop criteria (any one triggers rollback):
- Sustained P99 increase > 2x baseline for 10m and not explained by traffic pattern.
- Request-level error rate increase > 0.5% absolute at 5m window.
- TTF (token-level) P95 increase > 40% and KV-hit-rate drops > 15% concurrently.
- GPU stall / kernel OOM events observed in telemetry for the B pool.
- Latency differential concentrated in a single slice/cohort > suggestive of input-shape/pathological pattern.

Operator mitigation ladder (fast actions):
1) Pause ramp and reduce B allocation by half; re-evaluate 5m window.
2) If pause not enough, route 100% of failing slice back to A using route tag gating.
3) If slice unknown, shift entire cohort back to A and collect traces.
4) If systemic, flip global traffic to A and open incident with SRE.

Observability checklist (what to watch during run):
- P50/P95/P99 at request and token levels for both variants (A/B).
- Token-time heatmap by model step (embedding, decode, kv-lookup).
- KV cache hit-rate and cache eviction rate.
- Backpressure metrics: queue length, worker utilization, GPU SM utilization, device-side stalls.
- Request surface errors: inference exceptions, timeouts, truncated responses.
- Business metrics: conversion rate, downstream pipeline latency, any user-visible error reports.
- Sampling: capture 1% of full requests with full token traces to s3 for later analysis.

Telemetry priming and guardrails (implementation notes for eng):
- Ensure B exposes the same response headers with route, model-shim, and cache-tags so logs can be correlated.
- Add short TTL debug logs under experimental flag to avoid noise in production indices.
- On-call alert thresholds: set temporary alerts for +30% p95 and +50% p99 for the experiment route, auto-silenced after ramp completes.

Post-rollout retrospective (within 48h):
- Gather example traces for all stop-criteria triggers or near-miss windows.
- Run regression detector: token-level quality vs. baseline (LLM-quality eval subset).
- Cost review: change in token cost per 1000 requests and GPU utilization delta.
- Update experiment notes: what input shapes, prefixes, or slices caused issues and remediation actions.

Handy operator commands (examples, replace cluster/route names):
- Reduce allocation: rcli rollout adjust --route candidate-route --percent 2.5
- Snapshot latency: rcli metrics snapshot --route candidate-route --window 5m --percentiles 50,95,99
- Force route revert: rcli routing set --route candidate-route --variant control
- Enable debug sampling: rcli debug sample --route candidate-route --rate 0.01 --sink s3://redwood-debug/ab-2025-01-15

Human factors: coordination and comms
- Keep release chat thread pinned with header: owner, current allocation, last-checked times, and last action.
- Short cadence updates every 10m during ramp stages.
- If escalating, page SRE lead and product owner in first 5m.
- When rolling back, mention explicit rationale: metric name, window, and magnitude.

Open questions / follow-ups (notes-to-self):
- Do we need a separate low-latency-only routing tier in the runtime to isolate microsecond-sensitive requests?
- Can we auto-throttle B requests when average queue time > 20ms?
- Add a preflight synthetic that mirrors customer prefixes (to catch prefix-specific cache misses).
- Integrate a small per-experiment canary harness into the console UI for one-click pause/revert.

Appendix: quick sign-off template to paste into chat:
- Experiment: <short-name> | Owner: <name> | Start: <UTC> | Seed: 0.1% | Current: <x%> | Next: <y% in zm>
- Key baselines: p95=<ms>, p99=<ms>, token-ttf p95=<ms> | Stop-criteria configured: yes/no

End of scratchpad.
Notes: intentionally terse, meant for copy-paste into release docs. Keep this file as a living operator cheat-sheet; when stable, fold into canonical runbook.
